---
title: "Exercise. The four dplyr verbs with the Latvian Labour Force Survey"
format: html
---

Each part answers one question about work in Latvia in 2025. Codes are in `data/lfs_codebook.md`. Replace each `___` with code, remove `#| eval: false`, and write the answer under the chunk.

**Class 4:** parts A and B. **Class 5:** part C. **Class 6:** part D.

| Verb | What it does | Part |
|---|---|---|
| `filter()` | Extract specific observations (rows) | A |
| `select()` | Remove distracting columns | B |
| `mutate()` | Compute new variables | C |
| `summarise()` | Summarize cases | D |

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, here, janitor)
```

## Look first

```{r}
#| label: look
# One row per person. Blank cells mean "not applicable", "." is also read as missing
here("data", "lfs_2025_example.csv") |>
  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  glimpse()
```

# Part D. summarise(): summarize cases

The survey covers a sample. Each person has a weight (`Svars_G`), the number of people in Latvia that person stands for. Sum the weights to estimate people in Latvia. Use `Svars_G` for one year of data.

## D1. How many people aged 15 to 74 are employed, unemployed or inactive?

```{r}
#| label: d1
#| eval: false
# count(wt = ...) adds up the weights instead of counting rows

  read_csv(na = c("", ".", "NA"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  ___
```
